name: Sacsayhuamán Megalithic Citadel
description: Colossal zig-zag megalithic stone citadel overlooking Cusco, featuring individual polished limestone blocks weighing over 120 tonnes.
history: Served as the military fortress guarding the royal capital of Cusco and the ceremonial arena for the Inti Raymi (Festival of the Sun).
construction: Constructed with precision dry-stone ashlar masonry where massive polygonal stones fit together so tightly that a sheet of paper cannot pass between them.
architecture: Three tiers of zig-zagging stone terrace ramparts designed in the shape of lightning and the teeth of the Cusco puma.
significance: UNESCO World Heritage Site as part of the City of Cusco.
